front.title: Key Provenance Evidence for Certification Authority Keys

abstract.t: Many cryptographic modules can sign a statement that they generated a given key, using an attestation key that the module vendor certifies. This document defines Key Provenance Evidence (KPE), which applies this to the keys of certification authorities (CAs). A KPE file carries the public key of a CA together with the statements that modules signed about it. Anyone can then verify a chain of signatures from the vendor's trust anchor to the public key in a CA certificate, and so confirm that the private key was generated inside a module. The signed statements stay in the formats that module vendors already use, which are listed in a new IANA registry. Modules that are already deployed need no changes.
